findings.title: Override days skip busy checks and can be double-booked
findings.body: In checkIfIsAvailable, if any date override falls on the slot's day and the slot is treated as inside that override, the function returns true immediately. That return is before the busy-interval loop, so Google Calendar conflicts and existing Cal.com bookings are never consulted. isFixed is true for every user when schedulingType is null and for every collective host, and the same helper is used for fixed and round-robin hosts, so this is not limited to the round-robin case. On any day that has a date override, the public schedule can offer times when that host is already busy, which is what the booking page presents.

findings.title: Multiple override windows on one day remove all slots
findings.body: The new override scan uses dateOverrides.find and treats a truthy callback as "this slot is unavailable". The callback returns true when the slot is entirely before or entirely after that one window, and find stops at the first such window. A normal split override (for example 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00 on the same date) therefore rejects every slot, because every slot lies outside at least one window, and the day shows no availability. The predicate is also too weak in the other direction: it only excludes slots that end at or before the window start or start after the window end, so a slot that starts before the window and ends inside it is treated as bookable. Availability should require the whole slot to sit inside at least one same-day window.

findings.title: Working-hours recheck zeroes split schedules
findings.body: The new working-hours fallback uses the same inverted find, and it runs for every fixed host whenever an override did not already return — including ordinary single-host events, because those users are marked isFixed. workingHours.find rejects the slot if any entry for that UTC weekday does not contain the slot start. Two intervals on the same day (a lunch break is the common case) therefore eliminate every slot, including times that fall inside one of the intervals, so those hosts get an empty booking page. Separately, end is computed from slotStartTime rather than slotEndTime, so a slot that starts inside the range but runs past workingHour.endTime is accepted. That shows up in round-robin, where aggregated hours can emit a slot another host can take after this host's hours have ended. A weekday present in no workingHours entry is not rejected either, so this check cannot enforce a fixed host's day off.

findings.title: Blocked-day overrides are never recognized
findings.body: A fully blocked date is stored as an override whose start and end are the same instant, and this function tries to treat that as unavailable for the whole day. The check is dayjs(...) === dayjs(...). Those are two different objects, so reference equality is never true, even when both instants match. The later before/after checks then only exclude slots that do not overlap that single point, leaving a bookable hole around the shifted timestamp. For a UTC−5 host blocked at 00:00, the instant is shifted to 05:00Z, and a slot that overlaps 05:00Z is reported available on a day the host marked unavailable. Compare with isSame (or the underlying timestamps) and, on a match, reject the whole day.

findings.title: Override date match depends on the server timezone
findings.body: Whether an override applies is decided by comparing dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format("YYYY MM DD") to slotStartTime.format("YYYY MM DD"). slotStartTime is time.utc(), so its format is UTC. The left side is built with dayjs(date.start) in local mode, so format uses the Node process timezone. If that timezone is not UTC, an override whose shifted instant falls on a different local calendar date than its UTC date does not match the slot. US evening overrides, which land in the 00:00–04:00Z window, are the typical case: dateOverrideExist stays false and the override is silently ignored, so the fixed host is treated as on their normal hours. Both sides need to be formatted in UTC, or the day bounds compared as absolute instants.

findings.title: Override timezone conversion drops the day and double-applies DST
findings.body: Date overrides are stored as the organizer's wall-clock time encoded in a UTC timestamp (a 14:00 IST override is 14:00Z, which the existing tests rely on). The new code adds inviteeOffset − organizerOffset minutes and then keeps only .hour() and .minute(), so a result on the previous or next calendar day cannot be represented. A 20:00–23:00 organizer-UTC override viewed from UTC+3 becomes 23:00 and 02:00; end-minute 120 is less than start-minute 1380, buildSlots drops any range whose start is not before its end, and the host's normal hours for that day were already removed, so the attendee sees no slots instead of 23:00–02:00. A Tokyo 08:00 override is placed at 19:00 on the New York day that contains the raw 08:00Z value, which is the next New York date, not 19:00 the previous evening (the real instant, 08:00 JST). Those minutes are then passed through buildSlots's organizerDSTDiff − inviteeDSTDiff correction, which exists for values computed from today's offset; these minutes already used the offset at the override instant, so when the two zones are not in the same DST period versus today every override slot shifts by an extra hour. Offsets are read via dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone): Date#toString is implementation-defined, a failed parse yields NaN and the range is dropped, and a missing timeZone (optional on TimeRange) throws from .tz() and fails the whole schedule request. checkIfIsAvailable converts the same overrides a different way (subtract the organizer offset and compare absolute instants), so the two layers disagree and a cross-midnight override can be emitted by one and rejected by the other, blanking the day.

findings.title: Fixed-host override behavior is untested
findings.body: The only new assertion re-queries the same personal event — one host, one override window, no calendar busy time — in Asia/Dhaka and expects the same UTC instants as Asia/Kolkata. That does not cover fixed-host round-robin, which is the bug the PR says it fixes, nor two windows on one date, a blocked day (start equal to end), a busy conflict on an override day, a timezone gap that crosses midnight, or a DST boundary. createBookingScenario never attaches hosts to the mocked event type, and the host fixture is not the { isFixed, user } shape getSchedule reads, so the new fixed-host branch of checkIfIsAvailable cannot be exercised without harness changes. The new paths can drop all slots or ignore busy times while this test stays green.
